findings.where: 003:282-284 (§4.3 step 4); contradicts 003:614 and current code at gym_read_models.sql:9-15 and freeze_preview_binding.sql:20-29
findings.defect: The record looks up the operation ID and hash before checking tenant and role. Today both gym definers authorise first. Following §4.3 would let a revoked staff member or session replay stored finance outcomes. That regresses current code and breaks PRD §22.1 'staff role cache cannot extend revoked permission'
findings.fix: Order: identity + session → tenant/role scope → lock → replay lookup → write-rate count → dependencies → per-kind permission → base revision → validation → write. operation_result_v1 re-runs identity and tenant checks and returns NOT_FOUND otherwise

findings.defect: Reads are counted in the PostgREST pre-request function and stored in private.rate_windows. PostgREST runs GET/HEAD and STABLE/IMMUTABLE RPCs in READ ONLY transactions, and the pre-request function runs inside them. The counter write would fail (25006) on every direct table read that §4.2 still allows
findings.fix: The pre-request function only checks (contract header). Choose a read-limit mechanism that does not write inside the request transaction, or scope it to volatile POST RPCs. Add 'access mode of pre-request on GET' to §12

findings.defect: The server rejects only an unsupported major version, but 0.x allows breaking changes in a minor bump (including the G-5 decimal switch). An app built against 0.2 would be accepted by a 0.3 server with incompatible payloads until 1.0.0
findings.fix: In 0.x, compare MAJOR.MINOR (caret semantics). Publish the supported range in health-v1. CONTRACT_UNSUPPORTED applies to any version outside that range

findings.defect: amountMinor is limited to 0..100,000,000,000. Existing signed money fields fall outside it: gym_charge_adjustments.delta_paise and gym_allocations.delta_paise (check <>0; written negative at gym_read_models.sql:89,93,107), and the gym_balance net/credit values (gym_operations.sql:126), all returned by gym_account_v1
findings.fix: Define non-negative money (prices, payments) and signed money (±1e11 per row, sums bounded by Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). Name which fields use which

findings.defect: QA-1 F-8e is routed to 'outcomes store results, not snapshots'. Outcome rows already store only {id, revision} (member_operations.sql:103). F-8e (bootstrap-security-review.md:191) is the full session-plus-sets snapshot written to public.workout_revisions on every operation (scheduling_and_history.sql:93-96). The rule fixes nothing, and MB-4 would treat F-8e as resolved
findings.fix: Add a workout_revisions rule: set-level revision rows or diffs, or snapshot only on correction kinds, never on set.commit. Route it to MB-4

findings.defect: PRD §21.3's 'no staff health API' and 'owner/manager templates' constraints are dropped. §10 routes 'staff notes and the private-health boundary' to §6, but §6 has no such row. Linked members can currently read gym_members.notes through register_read (gym_operations.sql:108; QA-1 F-2), while PRD §22.3 treats these as staff-only
findings.fix: Add §6 rows: no staff endpoint returns member health or personal records; offers are owner/manager only; staff-only notes are not readable by the linked member (column grant or view) and are excluded from member export. Owners G17.api and G18.api

findings.defect: Checkpoint F-10 says every actor_id needs the SET NULL that §21.2 requires. PRD §21.2 (PRD:1406) requires SET NULL only on the gym link. SET NULL on actor_id is a destructive update to rows that 003 §3.3 makes immutable even to definers, and an immutability trigger would block the FK action anyway. 003 leaves actor-reference deletion undecided. Today, deleting an auth user with any personal row or staff action fails on NO ACTION foreign keys
findings.fix: Decide: actor references point at a retained non-personal actor key (minimal tombstoned profile or actor table) with RESTRICT; linked_user_id ON DELETE SET NULL; personal tables cascade from profiles or follow an explicit purge order. Correct checkpoint F-10

findings.defect: The per-account change_seq allocation is unspecified. A sequence or max()+1 lets a transaction that commits late fall behind a client cursor, so that client never receives the row. Member RPCs serialise on an advisory lock (function_lint_cleanup.sql:34), but transitional direct writes and gym writes to member-visible rows do not
findings.fix: Allocate from a per-account counter row updated in the same transaction (lock held until commit). Every writer to member-visible rows, gym commands included, stamps through it

findings.defect: PRD §22.1 (PRD:1481) requires an authorised proxy or revocable access where immediate revocation is needed, and §22.3 says 'revoke access immediately' on deletion. 003 makes 300-second signed URLs the only path, so gym documents for revoked staff and assets after deletion stay fetchable for up to 300 s. Future passport-link revocability is also not stated
findings.fix: Per bucket, state whether a 300 s residual is accepted or an Edge streaming proxy checks access on each request. Deletion purges objects. Passport links are independently revocable

findings.defect: Ten pending owner gates where AR-1 needs one approval of a concrete ADR. G-2 (as architecture), G-4, G-5, G-6, G-9 and G-10, plus the defaults in G-7 and G-8, are reversible engineering decisions the owner has already delegated. G-9 deletes four unexecuted draft files that git can restore. The test plan branches on G-9 and sends a non-empty diff to the owner
findings.fix: Make these Decisions in the ADR body, with G-1 as the single dated approval. List separately, as owner-reserved and unclaimed: region (Mumbai), account and plan purchase (OW-3), vendor adoption (RevenueCat, Sentry and its data region, MSG91/WhatsApp), legal (DEC-04), prices (DEC-06), AI vendor (DEC-08), photo backup (DEC-09). In phase 2, delete the four files after the comparison table and notify S2. A non-empty diff or CLI failure goes to the orchestrator; only a local db reset needs owner confirmation

findings.defect: Hashing the contract major turns a lost-response retry after an app update into OPERATION_REUSED. Dependencies are hashed as an ordered list. Once outcomes are pruned, the dependency check returns retryable DEPENDENCY_PENDING forever, which PRD §20.2 forbids ('not infinite retry')
findings.fix: Hash actor, scope, kind, entityId, baseRevision and payload; treat dependencies as a sorted set or leave them out. Keep applied operation IDs (without results) beyond 180 days, or make an expired dependency non-retryable. On OPERATION_REUSED, the client calls operation_result_v1 first

findings.defect: git diff --exit-code ignores untracked files. The snapshot and fixture are new, so the restore checks for M1.2, M1.4 and M4.3 prove nothing

findings.defect: toFixed rounds the binary double, not half away from zero on decimal ties. The '-0.000000' path is untested. A session with no eligible set gives volume 0 in TypeScript but NULL in SQL. No current vector hits these cases
